decisions.rationale: The item tests the explicit domestic-dignitary event-facility category. Q113 covers temporary designation around foreign dignitary visits, not this category.
The international-conference preparation/operation facility category is source-defined and distinct from generic temporary designation coverage.

Tier B PASS. The item tests legal-regime non-substitution: Aviation Act authorization does not itself satisfy Small UAV Act exception requirements. Decision authority, exception boundary and reasoning path differ from Q056/Q114.
The general statutory exception set is answer-unique and differs from Q056, which assumes an exception and tests notification, and Q114, which tests a narrowed airport/defense red-zone branch.
Immediate police enforcement powers during a prohibited flight are absent from the current canonical bank and are directly source-defined.
The red/yellow penalty distinction is tied to a source-defined legal classification and consequence boundary, not a number-only substitution. Q055 tests geography, not sanctions.
The weak-radio field-strength threshold determines classification and license/qualification consequence, making the quantitative value action-defining rather than low-value trivia.
The item correctly separates license-free operation from equipment technical-conformity obligations. Q057 assumes conformity and tests a different license comparison.
The dual requirement for amateur operator qualification and station license is distinct from Q115, which assumes both and tests prohibition on profit-motivated business use.
Tier B PASS. The secondary-service interference rule changes operation applicability and the decision boundary from business-purpose eligibility to spectrum-priority protection.
Location-specific coexistence action near 5.7GHz image systems and 5.8GHz DSRC/ETC is a distinct operational response not tested by existing amateur-radio questions.

The item tests the non-statutory but operationally relevant flight-restraint-request status and preflight response. Existing local-rule and general-constraint questions do not test this status distinction.
The one-year post-refusal/current-hold application boundary is source-defined and distinct from Q231 age eligibility and from the separate cancellation branch in C014.
The two-year post-cancellation/current-suspension application boundary is source-defined, answer-unique and materially distinct from the one-year refusal branch.
The item tests refusal/hold grounds after exam success, a separate issuance decision from exam sequence or practical-test exemption.
Exam misconduct consequences include immediate test/result effects and possible future testing refusal; existing exam questions do not cover this enforcement path.
Physical-condition restrictions attached to a certificate are a distinct operational condition from Q235 aircraft-type/flight-method limitations.

Tier B PASS. The post-issuance lifecycle state changes the solving rule: specified health, conduct or legal grounds can trigger cancellation or suspension after certificate issuance. This differs from Q199's generic sanction list and pre-application eligibility questions.
The item tests concrete flight-manual safety-management content within the Category II-B no-individual-permission route. Q049 tests only the top-level route conditions.
The three-year certificate validity horizon is the underlying lifecycle boundary; Q109 instead tests renewal-course and application timing windows.
